title: Progressive Emission Safety Net — PRD for structured output, tool handshake degradation, and streaming checkpoints
creator: Elena Park
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines the "Progressive Emission Safety Net": a set of behavioral requirements and acceptance tests for structured outputs and tool/function calling when responses are emitted progressively (streaming). The goal is to ensure consumer resilience across partial emits, schema drift, network interruptions, and downstream tool failures while providing clear observability and safe rollback modes.

Goals:
- Define a canonical lightweight handshake and checkpoint envelope for streamed structured output that consumers can rely on for incremental validation and replay.
- Specify graceful degradation modes for tool calls (timeboxed handshakes, replayable call intents, fallback descriptors).
- Provide testable acceptance criteria and telemetry signals to gate rollout.
- Minimize breaking changes for existing API users while enabling stronger guarantees for enterprise customers.

Scope:
In-scope: streaming text and framed structured emits (JSON fragments), function/tool invocation metadata, per-fragment provenance headers, checkpoints (sequence/offset), observable error classification, retry semantics for idempotent tool calls, examples and test harness.
Out-of-scope: model-level generation logic (LLM tokenization internals), SDK surface changes beyond exposing headers, policy/auth changes for tool endpoints (handled by ENG-28012).

Key assumptions:
- Clients can parse newline-delimited frames and accept optional metadata headers.
- Tool endpoints will support an idempotency token on the first handshake.
- Network interruptions may occur; we must provide resume semantics or well-defined finalization messages.

Handshake & checkpoint envelope (informal):
Each streamed frame contains either: a 'fragment' (partial object), a 'checkpoint' (sequence number + deterministic hash), or a 'final' message. Example frame payload (stringified for clarity):

{"type":"fragment","seq":12,"schema":"billing.v2.Invoice","payload":"{\"line_items\":[...]}","prov":{"model_version":"rdw-v1.9","prompt_hash":"abc123"},"idempotency_token":"r-550e8400"}

Checkpoint frame example:
{"type":"checkpoint","seq":12,"checkpoint_hash":"sha256:...","accepted_schema":"billing.v2.Invoice","partial_valid":true}

Behavioral requirements (high level):
- Consumers must be able to validate partial objects using the accepted_schema on checkpoint frames.
- If a checkpoint indicates partial_valid=false, the runtime should attach a remediation hint (suggested fallback model variant or retry policy).
- Tool calls invoked mid-stream must include a call-intent envelope (function name, args preview, idempotency token). The platform must guarantee at-least-once delivery semantics with clear duplicate suppression metadata for idempotent endpoints.

Error modes & degradation policies:
1) Network interruption between fragments: system emits 'resumeable' checkpoint with a TTL and resume token. Clients can request missing fragments via the control-plane within TTL.
2) Tool endpoint unavailable: function-call frame is marked 'deferred'. Runtime retries based on configured backoff; if retries exceed policy window, emit 'fallback' frame with best-effort result and explicit 'uncertain' flag.
3) Schema incompatibility on checkpoint: emit 'schema-mismatch' frame with suggested compatibility actions (coerce-to-string, fallthrough).

Telemetry & observability signals required:
- fragment_emit_rate (per model+route)
- checkpoint_acceptance_ratio (partial_valid true vs false)
- function_call_retries, function_call_duplicate_suppression_count
- resume_requests_per_minute and resume_success_rate
- fallback_emits_rate and customer-facing_fallback_rate

Rollout plan & gating:
- Alpha (internal): enable on canary routes for 2 teams, collect telemetry for 14 days, validate resume success > 95% and checkpoint acceptance > 98%.
- Beta (selected customers): opt-in for enterprise tenants behind Dedicated; require explicit SDK opt-in.
- GA: enable-by-default with feature flag for private deployments; rollout conditional on telemetry gates.

Files & artifacts referenced:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STR/Progressive+Emission+Safety+Net (internal doc with spec and sample harness)
- GitHub RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/218 (handshake protocol proposal)
- Test harness: internal repo rdw/inference-stream-test (unit & e2e scenarios)

Acceptance test plan summary (details below in acceptance_criteria): logs and golden fixtures for checkpoints, intentional failures to verify fallback frames and idempotency behavior, simulated network drop tests to validate resume semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint frames are emitted for any long-running structured emit where payload size > 16KB or after 30s of continuous emission; checkpoint contains seq, checkpoint_hash, accepted_schema.
Client-visible partial_valid metrics: >= 98% of checkpoints in normal traffic must be partial_valid=true in alpha canary (measured over 14-day window).
Resume token lifecycle: resume_token TTL enforced (default 10 minutes); resume API returns missing fragments exactly once per token; resume_success_rate >= 95% in test harness.

Function/tool call idempotency: first-call carries idempotency_token; repeated deliveries within 5-minute dedup window must be recognized by runtime and flagged as duplicate in telemetry but not re-executed for idempotent endpoints.

Deferred function semantics: when upstream tool returns 5xx or times out, runtime emits a 'deferred' then retries with exponential backoff up to policy limit; after exceed, runtime emits 'fallback' frame with 'uncertain':true and documented fallback_reason.

Schema mismatch handling: when checkpoint accepted_schema does not validate payload, runtime emits 'schema-mismatch' frame and attaches a single suggested remediation (coerce, simplify, or escalate) with deterministic ordering.
Observability: all frames emit trace_id and span_id headers; traces link to console-2026.04 UI; token-level cost and latency breakdown show per-frame token counts in Console's timeline view.
Backward compatibility: existing non-streaming clients receive a single 'final' frame equivalent to prior API behavior; no required client changes for non-streaming flows.
Security: idempotency tokens and resume tokens are treated as short-lived bearer tokens and logged only in redacted form; security review signoff required before Beta (security_review_required=true).
